security_spec.violation_condition: Linux KVM does not save/restore hstatus.MTAG_I on VM-entry/VM-exit, or OpenSBI/Linux does not save/restore mstatus.MTAG_I across M-mode trap handlers that use MPRV, causing stale MTAG_I values to incorrectly suppress or enable tag checks on HLV/HSV/MPRV memory accesses that cross security boundaries
security_spec.summary: New hstatus.MTAG_I and mstatus.MTAG_I bits act as opt-out overrides for tag checking on HLV/HSV/MPRV accesses; if the kernel or KVM fails to context-switch these bits, a guest code page's MTAG bit can leak across VM boundaries to suppress tag checks on hypervisor emulated accesses, letting a malicious guest bypass memory tagging on loads/stores emulated by the hypervisor

findings.finding: The RISC-V memory tagging extension (MTE) with hstatus.MTAG_I / mstatus.MTAG_I CSR fields for HLV/HSV/MPRV tag-check control does not exist in this Linux kernel tree. The hstatus register defined in csr.h (lines 135-153) contains only: HUPMM, VSXL, VTSR, VTW, VTVM, VGEIN, HU, SPVP, SPV, GVA, VSBE. No MTAG_I bit exists. The KVM hstatus save/restore in vcpu_exit.c:74 and vcpu.c:799-861 correctly uses csr_swap(CSR_HSTATUS, ...) for VM-entry/VM-exit, which would correctly preserve any hypothetical future MTAG_I field. The RISC-V privileged spec (hypervisor.adoc:167-220) defines the hstatus register with no MTAG_I field — the only MTE bit in the ISA manual is in mctrctl (smctr.adoc:38) for Control Transfer Recording, unrelated to memory tagging.

spec_citations.excerpt: The hstatus register is an HSXLEN-bit read/write register. Fields: VSBE, GVA, SPV, SPVP, HU, VGEIN, VTVM, VTW, VTSR, VSXL, HUPMM. No MTAG_I field is defined.

The hypervisor virtual-machine load and store instructions (HLV/HSV) are valid only in M-mode or HS-mode. Each instruction performs an explicit memory access with effective privilege VS or VU. Two-stage address translation is applied, and HS-level sstatus.SUM is ignored.
